scenes.sting: Miss Hartwell survives the Assembly. The ton waits to see what survival costs. The Hartwell–Drummond alliance — so unexpectedly, so visibly struck — prospers in ballrooms. Miss Honoria Drummond, sponsored, gowned, and much improved by the association, does her patroness credit. The patroness's gowns speak of settled accounts. Whether the accounts are in fact settled, the ton awaits to learn. Dragons, after all, keep ledgers — and ledgers, unlike ruins, are never proved engineered. They are merely presented. Miss Hartwell is expected to continue paying. In daylight. The ton will be watching the coin.

★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — HONORIA'S TRUTH. Honoria asks the question outright; Rose must decide what the girl is allowed to know about why she is being sponsored.

options.label: Tell her plainly
options.detail: *Honesty+, Honoria stricken but trusting.* "Your aunt holds a letter — a debt of my family's — and the price of her silence is your Season. I will not lie to you, Honoria. But I will also not fail you." She weeps, then straightens; the trust between them becomes iron.

options.label: Let her believe it's friendship
options.detail: *Kindness+, the lie accrues interest.* "Because I like you, and because the ton is wrong about you, and because someone ought to have done it sooner." She glows; and every kind hour afterward compounds the debt of the untruth.

options.label: Deflect, kindly
options.detail: *Wit+, the question waits.* "Because your aunt terrifies me slightly less than you terrify yourself, and I have always backed the braver horse." She laughs through the stammer; the question retreats, but it will return better armed.

★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — CECILIA'S LEAK. Rose confronts Cecilia — not at tea, but on the neutral ground of the park — and decides what becomes of the woman who retailed her sentences.

options.label: Cut her
options.detail: *Society+, Cecilia dangerous.* "You are not received at Hartwell House, nor at Augusta's, nor anywhere my name carries. The ton will notice. Let them." Cecilia's smile finally cracks; a cut enemy is an honest enemy — and a vengeful one.

options.label: Warn her
options.detail: *Wit+, she smiles.* "Do it again, and I will tell the ton exactly what you said, and where, and why — with the same fond smile you used on me. We understand each other." She laughs, genuinely delighted; the game between them is now declared, and therefore almost honorable.

options.label: Feed her false words
options.detail: *Cunning+, the trap is set.* "You love a private sentence, Cecilia. Here is another: tell Lady Calthorpe that I said Honoria is to marry imminently — to whom, I cannot say. Watch what the ton does with it, and wonder why I told *you*." Cecilia glows; the lie is launched, and its fuse is in Rose's hand.

options.label: Task Élise to listen
options.detail: *Intelligence+, the atelier becomes an ear.* "Then listen — deliberately. Who orders, who cannot pay, whose man asks after old coats. Bring it all to me, and I will make it worth the hearing." Élise nods slowly; the order book gains an invisible column, and the war gains its listening post.

options.label: Keep it casual
options.detail: *Charm+, the gossip comes unforced.* "No orders. No tasks. Just — if the workroom hears things, as workrooms do, I would like to hear them too. As a friend." Élise smiles; the intelligence will come, but on friendship's schedule, not war's.

options.label: Keep the atelier out of the war
options.detail: *Honor+, Élise's relief.* "No. Your workroom is a sanctuary — brides, bankrupts, fools, all confessed in safety. I will not make it a weapon." Élise exhales, and something in her face softens; the atelier stays clean — and Rose fights with one ear fewer.

The Hartwell heiress — so long the ton's puzzle in her plain muslins, propriety or poverty, never quite decided — has been seen at Trelawney's table, and at the White Hart after it, in company no heiress keeps by accident. Four banking houses, one young lady, and a gravity of manner the ton has not previously had the pleasure of pricing. What is pooled at a banker's dinner? Nerve, one hears. Bath holds its breath — decoratively, of course. The season's account is stated: money traced, blood drawn, price paid — and a price, hanging, acknowledged before witnesses and carried, honestly, into the seasons to come.
